newsitem.title: UK: UK bookmakers cut odds on Labour election win.
newsitem.headline: UK bookmakers cut odds on Labour election win.

text.p: Bookmakers William Hill cut the odds on the opposition Labour party winning the next election to 1-3 from 2-5 in the aftermath of Labour leader Tony Blair's speech to his party's conference.
The odds on the ruling Conservatives winning the election, due by May 1997, were lengthened to 2-1 from 7-4.
"Punters were very impressed with the speech and were quick to begin backing Labour for the election," said a William Hill's spokesman.
